headline: SpaceX falters. Serbia commits. Defense funding grows.
deck: This week saw SpaceX's launch woes and Serbia's lunar ambitions, alongside a surge in defense funding.

stories.head: True Anomaly raises $190M in Series C
stories.body: True Anomaly secured a $190 million Series C funding round, reaching a valuation of $1.6 billion. The company focuses on co-orbital security and space domain awareness, with strong backing from the DoD. This cash influx highlights the military's increasing reliance on commercial capabilities for national security.
stories.soWhat: In an era where cash trumps innovation, True Anomaly’s funding suggests that the military-industrial complex is more interested in buying solutions than developing them in-house.

stories.head: US Space Force boosts budget by $1.4B
stories.body: The FY27 budget markup added $1.4 billion to the space resilience line, signaling a commitment to fortifying U.S. space capabilities. This increase comes as geopolitical tensions rise, emphasizing the need for robust space defense systems. Expect more contractors to vie for these funds as the government seeks to bolster its space posture.
stories.soWhat: This budget boost is a clear signal that the U.S. government is finally recognizing that space isn’t just a playground for billionaires, but a critical domain that needs serious investment.

stories.head: Sierra Space's Dream Chaser clears design review
stories.body: Sierra Space's Dream Chaser variant for the Department of Defense has successfully passed its critical design review. While this is a step forward, the spacecraft still has yet to demonstrate its capabilities in orbit. The military’s interest in this vehicle underscores the growing demand for versatile transport solutions in space.
stories.soWhat: Passing a design review is like getting a gold star in kindergarten; it’s nice, but we still need to see if the kid can actually play.

watchlist.title: SpaceX's next launch attempt
watchlist.body: After aborting the Starship Flight 13 launch, SpaceX's next attempt will be closely watched for any signs of improvement or further issues.

watchlist.title: Serbia's Artemis Accords implications
watchlist.body: Serbia's signing of the Artemis Accords may lead to increased European collaboration in lunar exploration, impacting future contracts and partnerships.

watchlist.title: Palantir's TITAN program extension
watchlist.body: With a $480 million extension, Palantir's TITAN program will be scrutinized for its effectiveness in delivering actionable intelligence to the military.

watchlist.title: Anduril and L3Harris constellation bid
watchlist.body: The collaboration between Anduril and L3Harris on a tactical SDA constellation could reshape defense procurement strategies moving forward.

talent.statLabel: Job orders YoY · plus 2 starters per head, an 8-year first
talent.head: Demand has doubled. So has our hit rate.
talent.body: EVONA's job orders are up 2.0× year-over-year, and for the first time in our eight-year history we're placing two new starters per EVONA staff member. The first number says demand is real. The second says we're converting it, which in recruitment is the only number that actually matters. Growth is heaviest in Series B/C startups; primes are running flat. Compensation isn't the variable. The constraint is schedule risk in the primes: senior engineers leave Boeing, Lockheed, Northrop because they want to ship hardware before retirement.
